papers.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
papers.abstract: Brown dwarfs are rare as close companions to stars compared to planets and stellar companions, a paucity known as the brown dwarf desert. Whether the desert sits at a fixed companion mass or a fixed companion-to-star mass-ratio $q$ has been difficult to test, because microlensing, radial velocities, and direct imaging have sampled comparatively narrow slices of stellar mass and separation. Here we apply a novel joint-modelling method to Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry from 63,254 stars to complete this picture with a sample 1-2 orders of magnitude larger than those of previous wide-orbit demographic studies. For the first time, we present a single survey that measures occurrence rates of both planetary and stellar companions on 3--94 yr orbits ($\sim$2--20\,au) across host masses from M dwarfs to B stars. We find that the desert is a mass-ratio feature: companions are strongly depleted at $q\approx2\%$ independent of stellar mass from M to B stars, and a desert at fixed companion mass is excluded. Furthermore, we find a positive trend in occurrence with metallicity below the mass-ratio desert, but a negative trend above. The desert therefore separates two distinct populations, plausibly two formation channels, that each scale with stellar mass: the lightest stellar-like companions of K stars ($\sim13 \, M_{jup}$) are less massive than the heaviest planet-like companions of B stars ($\sim27, M_{jup}$), which continue well beyond the deuterium-burning limit. Mass-ratio, not mass, is therefore the physically meaningful boundary between planets and their stellar-like counterparts.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Black Holes: Non-Gaussianity and Accretion Evade $μ$-Distortion Constraints
papers.abstract: Recent JWST observations of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$ suggest the existence of early supermassive black holes (SMBHs) with masses $\gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$. Their rapid emergence challenges conventional seeding and growth scenarios based on accretion and mergers of Population III stellar remnants, motivating renewed interest in primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from primordial perturbations. Explaining such massive seeds requires power spectrum enhancements that are constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) spectral distortions. In this work we perform the first comprehensive Bayesian exploration of non-Gaussian primordial perturbations capable of producing SMBH seeds while remaining consistent with CMB spectral distortion constraints, and examine the role of accretion history in constraining these models. We perform a suite of Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses of power spectrum enhancements (lognormal and cut-power-law) with varying local non-Gaussianity and accretion histories, satisfying the COBE/FIRAS $μ$-distortion constraint with and without the requirement that the model produces SMBH seeds. We find that both models can seed LRDs and evade $μ$-distortion bounds for $|f_{\rm NL}|= O(1)$ and peak amplitude $A= O(10^{-3})$, when standard Eddington-limited accretion is also incorporated. Interestingly, the results exhibit a preference for both positive and negative values of $f_{\rm NL}$. The preference for negative $f_{\rm NL}$ is strongly dependent on the accretion history, and is removed if the black holes have a small duty cycle, $f_{\rm duty}\lesssim 0.1$. These results demonstrate that the JWST high-$z$ LRD population can be seeded by primordial perturbations while remaining compatible with CMB data, and highlight the importance of next-generation CMB spectral distortion missions to test this hypothesis.

papers.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe foreground ionized baryons via their dispersion measures (DM). Using 1748 sub-arcminute-localized sources from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog, we conduct a statistical stacking study of the circumgalactic media (CGM) of nearby galaxies by analyzing the DMs of FRBs whose sightlines intersect foreground halos. For galaxy halos within 50 Mpc, we measure a mean DM excess of $119\pm44$ pc~cm$^{-3}$ $(p = 0.0053; \sim 2.6σ)$ within one virial radius. Expanding to 150 Mpc (628 intersections), we find a tentative decline in the mean DM as a function of impact parameter $(p = 0.0046; \sim 2.6σ)$, which is predominantly driven by typical Milky Way (MW)-like galaxies $(10 \leq \log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq 11)$. We use this DM profile to constrain parameters of the CGM electron density distribution, $n_e^\mathrm{CGM}(r) \propto r^{-3β}$, finding an extrapolated central electron density in the range of $(1.7-21.1) \times 10^{-3}\mathrm{\,cm}^{-3}$, with a radial power-law index of $β= 0.68^{+0.15}_{-0.16}$, consistent with constraints from X-ray stacking studies of MW-like galaxies. At very low impact parameters, we detect a significant DM deficit likely due to cross-matching FRBs that originate from galaxies within our galaxy sample. By deriving the DM-galaxy cross-correlation function, we show that this deficit matches theoretical predictions if 20 FRBs originate from galaxies within 150 Mpc, indicating that CHIME/FRB detects a higher fraction of low-$z$ FRBs than previously thought. We forecast that $10^4$ FRBs with similar localization errors will provide a 5-$σ$ detection of the CGM, and that FRBs at intermediate redshifts ($0.4\lesssim z_\mathrm{FRB}\lesssim 0.75$) are ideal for studying intervening CGMs.

papers.title: Forward modeling linear variable filter data: High resolution PAH and Paschen-$α$ maps from SPHEREx
papers.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission is a powerful tool for the study of the interstellar medium (ISM) in both Galactic and extragalactic contexts. It can reveal ionization state, radiation field, metallicity, composition, and ISM structure as sculpted by processes like turbulence and stellar feedback. Here we use NASA's SPHEREx to produce clean, high-resolution PAH maps at spectral resolution R $\sim$ 35 (compared to WISE at R $\sim$ 2). Prior treatments of the SPHEREx linear variable filter data seek to convert them to more conventional band-averaged maps that can leave striping artifacts associated with spatially variable wavelength sampling, especially at emission lines. In contrast, we deliver a scalable forward-modeling method capable of generating high-quality all-sky SPHEREx emission-line maps at 8.5 arcsec FWHM angular resolution (on 6.4 arcsec pixels), while naturally producing maps without visible striping. We reformat the data into a pixel-level database, mask stellar contamination, and infill missing pixels with a conditional, data-driven, anisotropic Gaussian process. We apply our method to produce 3.3 $μ$m and 3.4 $μ$m PAH and Paschen-$α$ emission maps of a set of fields spanning a range of Galactic and extragalactic conditions including the Rosette nebula, the Corona Australis molecular cloud, M33, and M31. We demonstrate the quality and synergies of our SPHEREx 3.3 $μ$m PAH maps by comparisons with other available gas and dust tracer maps and achieve sensitivities up to $σ(I_{3.3}) = 2.7 \times 10^{-8}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ sr$^{-1}$. We estimate that a two-year extension of the SPHEREx survey, with modest modifications to the scanning strategy, would match or exceed the PAH sensitivity of WISE over the whole sky.

papers.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
papers.abstract: The XRISM X-ray Observatory has revealed evidence for a "double-cascade" scenario in the Perseus cluster, in which active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback and mergers drive turbulence over distinct radial ranges and spatial scales. Whether this gas kinematic feature is common among cool-core clusters remains unclear. Here, we revisit XRISM observations of A1795 and A2029 to investigate the signatures of AGN feedback and their contribution to the gas velocity fields. In A1795, AGN feedback dominates the velocity dispersion in the core, similar to Perseus, and may provide turbulent heating at a rate comparable to radiative cooling. In contrast, we obtain only an upper limit on the AGN feedback contribution in A2029, where merger-driven motions dominate. Tailored simulations indicate that an off-axis minor merger $\simeq1.6$ Gyr ago displaced the central low-entropy gas in A2029, potentially suppressing AGN activity. This gas is now returning to the center, possibly facilitating the re-establishment of AGN feedback. We propose an evolutionary view of the double-cascade scenario, in which merger-driven motions dominate during and shortly after significant mergers, while feedback-driven turbulence re-emerges in cluster cores as systems relax. This framework provides a basis for interpreting XRISM kinematic measurements of (weak) cool-core clusters. Our findings highlight the importance of spatially resolved gas kinematics and detailed modeling for identifying double-cascade features and disentangling the contributions of AGN feedback and mergers.

papers.title: Joint Gaia-Hipparcos astrometry, RV, and Imaging posteriors from the G23H Hipparcos sample
papers.abstract: We present uniform posteriors indicating the presence or absence of stellar and planetary companions over a sample of $10^5$ stars in Hipparcos and Gaia. We use the "G23H" catalog to fit a model that incorporates absolute astrometry constraints from Hipparcos, Gaia DR2, and Gaia DR3, as well as Gaia DR3 photometry, excess RV variability, and includes information from the presence or absence of common-proper motion companions. The resulting posteriors can be used directly to detect new companions, to target RV and imaging follow-up observations, and for downstream demographics studies. We highlight example detections of known and new candidate companions and the companion detection rate across the HR diagram. The modelling approach we present is directly applicable to Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry and RVs. All posteriors are provided as a machine-readable catalog and user-accessible website http://exopo.st/.

papers.title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

papers.title: Coupled dark energy and apparent phantom crossing: a potential-independent lower bound
papers.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernovae, prefer a dark energy whose equation of state was below $-1$ in the past and is above $-1$ today. A canonical scalar field cannot cross this line, but it can appear to do so if it is coupled to dark matter, and we ask how strong this coupling must be, for any potential. We show that the apparent crossing requires the dark matter to lose a minimum fraction of its mass after recombination, fixed by the expansion history $H(z)$. For a constant coupling $β=d\ln m/dφ$, the mass can change only as fast as the field moves, and the speed of the field is itself set by $H(z)$, so that the coupling must be larger than a minimum value $β_{\rm min}[H(z)]$. This bound holds for any potential, applies to the largest value of the coupling when the coupling depends on the field, and is reached exactly when the field comes to rest within the observed range. For the DESI DR2 best fits, the dark matter must lose about 5-7% of its mass by $z\simeq 0.8$, which requires $β_{\rm min}=0.047$-$0.058$; including the uncertainties of the data, the public DESI DR2 chains give the 95% lower limit $|β|>0.025$-$0.038$. We also apply the bound to published fits of coupled quintessence: all of them respect it, and those with a constant coupling reproduce only a shallow version of the crossing. Since the coupling cannot be smaller than $β_{\rm min}$, two known effects of the coupling have a minimum size: an extra attraction between dark matter particles of at least a few tenths of a per cent of gravity, and a lensing signal at least a few per cent weaker than the clustering of dark matter would suggest.

papers.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.abstract: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $Δ^2_{h,2}/Δ^2_h\simeq0.04\,Δ^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $Δ^2_ζ=c_wΔ_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4ε$, and $n_T=-2ε$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $ζ$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $μ$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.

papers.title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
papers.abstract: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $ξ=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $ΔN_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.

papers.title: The Cool Circumgalactic Echo of the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relatio
papers.abstract: The stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR), a key prediction of galaxy formation models, peaks at $M_* \sim 3 \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. This scale is often attributed to circumgalactic baryonic feedback processes, however, direct observational evidence linking the two remains scarce. Using Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) galaxy--quasar pairs, we map the cool circumgalactic medium (CGM) using Mg II $λ\lambda2796, 2803$ absorption with stacking technique across nearly three decades in stellar mass. The radial Mg II absorption equivalent-width profile, $W_{\rm MgII} \propto D^k$, becomes progressively shallower with increasing stellar mass, following $k = 0.70\log(M_*/M_\odot)-9.12$. Crucially, we find that the $W_{\rm MgII}$ in the CGM scales tightly with the SHMR. The $W_{\rm MgII}$ peaks at the same characteristic mass as the SHMR, coinciding with a transition of the cool CGM from super-virial to sub-virial kinematics. Low-mass halos show excess non-gravitational motions consistent with recycled accretion and feedback-driven circulation, whereas massive halos show halo-centric heating that may maintain star formation quenching. This study bridges the gap between cool CGM and SHMR, showing that peak star formation efficiency coincides with the most abundant cool CGM reservoirs.

papers.title: GRB 241030A: A fallback-accreting magnetar description of the early X-ray emission
papers.abstract: The bright, variable early X-ray emission of GRB~241030A at $z=1.411$ motivates investigating continued central-engine activity before the smoother afterglow emerges. We model a possible underlying magnetar contribution to the unabsorbed 0.3--10~keV XRT flux over 80--430~s, evolving the spin under fallback-disk and electromagnetic torques. A descriptive estimate gives $P_0\simeq4.25$~ms, $B\simeq3.04\times10^{15}$~G and source-frame $t_{\rm fb}\simeq143$~s, with exploratory temporal-block uncertainty ranges. The effective efficiency reaches its geometry-dependent ceiling of 81.2. At observer time 200~s, this realization has $P_*\simeq4.82$~ms and magnetospheric, corotation and light-cylinder radii $r_{\rm m}\simeq235$~km, $r_{\rm co}\simeq48$~km and $r_{\rm LC}\simeq230$~km. It is on the ejector branch; light-cylinder entry near 255~s initiates negative propeller torque and steepens the decline. The smooth component declines throughout the fitted interval; additional variable emission contributes to the observed maximum near 180~s. A correlated-residual Bayesian analysis permits a fainter component and broader dynamical histories, with median $P_0=16.8$~ms and central 68 per cent interval 2.76--286~ms. However, posterior predictive checks reveal that this statistical description typically underpredicts the observed flux level and variability, limiting its physical interpretation. Fallback-modified magnetar activity remains a possible descriptive scenario, but these analyses do not establish a unique underlying component or robust constraints on the initial spin and disk-interaction history. We also discuss Lense-Thirring precession and alternative mechanisms as possible origins of the early X-ray variability.

papers.title: Three-dimensional radiative transfer modeling of the scattering polarization in the solar H$α$ line
papers.abstract: The H$α$ line probes the solar chromosphere, but its scattering polarization is difficult to interpret because of magnetic fields, plasma motions, and atmospheric 3D inhomogeneities. We investigate its intensity and linear polarization in a 3D magnetohydrodynamic solar-atmosphere model including nonequilibrium hydrogen ionization. Using PORTA, we solve the full 3D non-LTE polarized radiative transfer problem for a multilevel hydrogen atom, accounting for atomic polarization, Hanle depolarization, horizontal radiative transfer, and macroscopic velocities. We degrade synthetic Stokes profiles to the spatial, spectral, and polarimetric resolution of ZIMPOL observations for direct comparison. The modeled center-to-limb variation follows the observed trend, with comparable polarization amplitudes. The profiles show large spatial variability from symmetry breaking by horizontal inhomogeneities and atmospheric dynamics, as well as diverse line-core asymmetries. Classifying $Q/I$ profiles by asymmetry reveals a statistical correlation between profile morphology and magnetic-field strength in the H$α$ formation region, consistent with Hanle depolarization: multi-peaked profiles favor stronger fields, whereas asymmetric single-peaked profiles favor weaker fields with smaller vertical strength variations. Thus, H$α$ scattering polarization reflects the interplay of magnetic fields, velocity gradients, and 3D radiative transfer. Our results highlight the need for 3D modeling to interpret H$α$ spectropolarimetry and its potential to diagnose chromospheric magnetism and dynamics.

papers.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abstract: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The final ray-traced spectrum, computed through photoionization code with Comptonization, accounts for both: emitted and reflected components. As a result, the strength of the SXE depends on the radial extend of the warm corona, i.e., its outer edge. We show that the radial transition from warm corona to disk atmosphere is governed by line cooling. By moving away from a central black hole Compton cooling is gradually replaced by line cooling, and the temperature drops sharply in vertical direction at a narrow iron ionization front, where iron ions Fe \textsc{xxv}--Fe \textsc{xxvi} recombine to Fe \textsc{xvii}. Notably, this transition takes place at a particular value of internal heating $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-23}$ erg cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, regardless of the Eddington ratio. We show, that at the given metal abundance, the SXE emitting area is larger for a higher accretion rate, in agreement with recent findings in changing look AGN. The overall emission spectrum from a warm corona is featureless, and the only iron K$_α$ line comes from a reflection. The line is stronger and more gravitationally distorted for a lower accretion rate, which is a direct result of the size of the warm corona. Furthermore, by increasing the iron abundance, the iron ionization front moves closer towards black hole, and a stronger iron line complex is emitted locally.

papers.title: Investigating the timescales traced by dynamical ages in young stellar systems
papers.abstract: Stars form in clustered environments, and then the stars may congregate into star clusters. The timescale on which individual stars form is not necessarily the same as the timescale on which star clusters assemble. Therefore, developing methods to probe these different timescales is a crucial part of understanding star cluster assembly and early evolution. Dynamical ages can be constructed from the kinematics of individual stars in clusters in the solar neighborhood using Gaia data. Using a star formation simulation, we test five different dynamical age methods. We divide dynamical ages into two approaches: methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster, and methods which trace the trajectories of individual stars. We confirm that size methods cannot accurately derive ages in bound clusters whereas methods tracing individual stars can be applied to both bound and unbound systems. We find that different dynamical age methods trace different epochs of star cluster formation and assembly: The method using stars with the oldest traceback ages provides an upper limit on stellar ages and the method using the median traceback ages is the best proxy for isochronal ages. Methods which trace the size evolution of the cluster best trace the onset of cluster expansion. Our work suggests that the median traceback time of stars moving away from the cluster provides the most reliable proxy for isochronal age, and that this method can be applied to any expanding system.

papers.title: A Many-Shapes framework for Galactic Cosmic Rays
papers.abstract: Thanks to recent measurements by space and ground-level detectors, the energy spectra of cosmic ray protons and helium nuclei are now known with good precision over a broad energy range extending for more than six orders of magnitude, from a few GeV to approximately 10PeV. These measurements reveal that both spectra do not have a simple power--law form, and exhibit several features. The proton to helium ratio exhibits a very unexpected behavior: it decreases for rigidities $\lesssim 10^5$~GV, and increases for higher rigidities. Several authors have interpreted the observed spectral features as revealing the fact the CR spectra are formed by the contributions of a few components (in some cases as few as two) produced by sources that belong to distinct classes of astrophysical accelerators, with sources in the same class producing spectra with the same characteristic shape. Most of these authors also consider it necessary to include the contribution of one (or perhaps more than one) ``local'' sources, recently active in the vicinity of the solar system. However, this approach has several limitations, and in this work we discuss an alternative scenario in which the cosmic ray sources, even belonging to the same class, produce spectra with a broad range of shapes. The power--law form of the total source spectrum emerges as the average of these contributions. In this framework observable spectral features can be produced by statistical fluctuations, and different spectral slopes for protons and helium nuclei can be observed even if one assumes that acceleration is rigidity-dependent.

papers.title: BAO and Type Ia Supernovae in LTB Cosmology: Constraints on Radial Inhomogeneity and Acoustic-Ruler Evolution
papers.abstract: We investigate how baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia supernovae constrain radial density profiles and acoustic-ruler evolution in Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) cosmology with a cosmological constant. Extending a homogeneous Friedmann-Robertson-Walker analysis requires calculating both distances and unequal radial and transverse stretching of a single initial ruler. Combining transverse BAO with supernovae isolates relative ruler evolution without an absolute calibration, while radial BAO supplies complementary information. We connect this test to exact nonlinear models with a low-density region compensated by surrounding excess matter, varying its depth, width, distance from the observer, and background matter density. Using DESI DR2 BAO and DES-Dovekie supernovae with full covariance and identical calibration freedom, the LTB fit improves $χ^2$ by 8.523 over flat $Λ$CDM for three additional parameters, mainly through the supernovae. DESI strongly rejects the particular deep profile favored by supernovae and angular BAO alone. However, a narrow depression near the observer and a broader, shallower depression farther away fit almost equally well, with $Δχ^2=0.647$. The combined data therefore constrain particular geometries without uniquely reconstructing the density profile or ruler evolution. The inference is conditional on supernova selection and interpreting released BAO summaries through local ruler transport at effective redshifts. Homogeneous simulations show that the fit improvement does not establish a detection of inhomogeneity. Finally, in the local approximation, common LTB ruler evolution shifts angular BAO and the transverse component of three-dimensional BAO together and cannot alone explain their discrepancy.

papers.title: Binary pulsar studies with multi-wavelength sky surveys. II. Companion star follow ups
papers.abstract: The identification of the stellar companions to binary pulsars and the extraction of the physical information encoded in their optical spectra are key to study the evolution of the binary system and how this is influenced by the interactions between the two stars. Obviously, extending the characterisation of the companion star spectra over an as large as possible wavelength range allows one to maximise the amount of information. In Paper I, we used 11 source catalogues built upon multi-wavelength (optical, infrared, ultraviolet) imaging sky surveys to search for the stellar companions of 144 field binary pulsars (i.e. not in Globular Clusters) selected from the Australia Telescope National Facility (ATNF) pulsar catalogue. For nine of these pulsars, for which the companion star had been already identified, we obtained new spectral information from imaging photometry in the surveys' bands. In particular, for some of these pulsars we provided the first possible detections of the companion star in either the ultraviolet or mid-infrared. Here, we serve this additional flux information as a base to update the spectral energy distribution (SED) of the companion stars and the multi-epoch catalogue photometry to look for flux modulation at the orbital period of the binary system.

papers.title: Long before plunge: Uncovering intermediate-mass black holes through their inspiralling compact object companions with LISA
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will provide novel capability to discover and study intermediate-mass (~$10^2-10^5 M_\odot$) black holes at the centres of dwarf galaxies and in dense stellar environments. We systematically map out the LISA-detectable parameter space of binaries consisting of a low-mass compact object spiralling into an intermediate-mass black hole (mass ratio ~$10^{-5} - 10^{-2}$) on equatorial orbits with generic eccentricity. The depth of the LISA survey reaches a redshift ~$5$ ($0.1$) for binaries with a primary black hole mass $m_1$ ~$10^4 M_\odot$ ($10^3 M_\odot$). If the orbital companion is a white dwarf, which could be disrupted prior to plunge, LISA's survey depth is well matched to (and, in many cases, exceeds) the one of electro-magnetic surveys. Although the maximum distance at which a source can be detected depends weakly on the orbital eccentricity, the latter strongly affects the portion of the binary inspiral over which a source is detectable. The instrument's sensitivity time-volume varies by many orders of magnitude depending on the binary's component masses: it reaches ~$1 - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$ (~$10^{-2} - 10^3 Gpc^3 yr$) for the more massive systems with $m_1 = 10^5 M_\odot$ ($10^4 M_\odot$) and decreases to ~$10^{-4} - 1 Gpc^3 yr$ for lighter primary black holes with $m_1 = 10^3 M_\odot$. Importantly, from tens of percent to the overwhelming majority of the total sensitivity time-volume (and therefore number of potential detections) comes from sources that do not plunge during the yr-long mission lifetime and are observed at an earlier stage of their inspiral. Despite the poorly known merger rates of this class of sources, our results show that LISA could identify from a handful to ~$10^3$ intermediate-mass black holes providing a new observational avenue for studying these elusive objects and the environments in which they reside.

papers.title: The Connection between Halo Assembly History and the Stellar Distribution II: A Radially Stratified Fossil Record of Past Halo Mass
papers.abstract: The spatial stellar distribution in massive central galaxies preserves a stratified fossil record of their host halos' assembly history. Using a halo-mass-complete sample from the IllustrisTNG-300 hydrodynamical simulation at $z=0.4$, we quantify this connection with two diagnostics. The fossil correlation $\tildeρ(z)$ measures how strongly a present-day galaxy property retains information about the progenitor halo mass at each redshift. The rank retention fraction $f_{\rm ret}(z)$ measures how many halos selected by that property today were among the most massive halos at each epoch. The central stellar mass at different galactocentric radii exhibits non-monotonic fossil correlations with past halo mass, peaking at intermediate redshifts that systematically shift from $z\sim1$ in the inner regions to $z\sim0.7$ in the outer stellar halos. These peak redshifts are robust from group to cluster scales. Partial correlations with halo accretion rate show that each peak marks the end of the epoch when that component's buildup was sensitive to halo accretion. The rank retention fraction shows that the annular stellar masses of the central galaxy beyond 10 kpc are less biased tracers of the most massive halos at intermediate redshifts than richness. This stratified fossil record originates mainly from the ex-situ phase of galaxy assembly. The outer stellar halo also traces the satellite population at intermediate redshift better than present-day richness. These results establish that the stellar profile of massive central galaxies encodes a radially stratified fossil record of halo assembly history.

papers.title: Revisiting the Einstein Cross with X-shooter spectra: New estimates of accretion disk parameters and broad emission line profiles from microlensing
papers.abstract: We present a spectroscopic study of the lensed quasar Q2237+0305, the Einstein Cross, assessing the best wavelength coverage to date with the X-shooter instrument (from $3000$ to $20000$ $\mathring{A}$), and thus improving the available spectroscopic data for this system. Using as a reference the characteristic emission lines for each quasar macro-image, we estimate the chromatic microlensing effect between pairs of images and calculate the extinction curve, confirming no significant differences between spectra $C$ and $A$ caused by extinction in the lens galaxy. In addition, we model the accretion disk characterized by a temperature profile with logarithmic slope $1/p$ and size $r_{s}$, assuming a thin-disk model with a power-law function of the form $r_{s}$ $\propto$ $λ^{p}$. To do this, we calculated a set of three chromatic microlensing measurements compiling previous estimates from the literature to test the wavelength dependence. This temperature profile was also compared to the canonical thin-disk model with $p=4/3$. Finally, we estimated the likelihood between the disk model and the observed data collected from multiple epochs through mock microlensing magnification maps and determined the probability density functions of each parameter from a Bayesian analysis. As a result, our estimated values for the accretion disk size and its exponential index are $r_{s}=4.9^{+2.3}_{-2.6}$ $\sqrt{M/0.3M_{\odot}}$ (lt-day) and $p=0.77^{+0.47}_{-0.28}$, respectively, reinforcing a departure from the standard accretion disk model ($ T \propto r_s^{-3/4}$).

papers.title: Parker Solar Probe Flies Through the Sun's Magnetic Poles Near 10 Solar Radii
papers.abstract: During the peak of the Sun's magnetic cycle, the solar corona can be complex and dominated by dynamics, while hidden below, the dipole component of the its photospheric magnetic field steadily reverses with respect to the rotational axis. Here, we use Parker Solar Probe (\emph{Parker}) data from two of its closest approaches in mid-2025 to show that the large-scale field at solar maximum resembled a simple tilted dipole. Similar to how Ulysses provided a complete scan of the solar rotation-aligned dipole at solar minimum, \emph{Parker} sampled the full range of magneto-latitudes, probing both magnetic poles below the Alfvén surface. Concurrent in situ data at larger distances reveal that both hemispheres contain solar wind with asymptotic speeds near 800 km s-1, yielding a picture similar to the Ulysses latitude scans but now in the equator near solar maximum. This contrasts with the disordered structure observed by Ulysses during its solar maximum latitude scan, which we attribute to the long timescale of data collection. Overall, we find the coronal field is organized as a dipole, but the fast solar wind streams are deformed by non-dipolar substructure: the positive dipole axis is aligned with one coronal hole, the negative centers over a pseudostreamer, and significant mass flux enhancements are observed at magnetic separatrixes. Our measurements suggest that even at solar maximum, the solar corona can still exhibit structure nearly as ordered as solar minimum. Moreover, by sampling rapidly and close to the Sun, the detailed imprint of source region structure can be determined in the solar wind.

papers.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of early-type stars. Testing Stokes parameter inversions with theoretical magnetohydrodynamic models
papers.abstract: Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI) is widely used to reconstruct magnetic fields in early-type stars from time-series spectropolarimetric observations, yet its accuracy has not been systematically validated against physically self-consistent, complex magnetic field models. We aim to assess the reliability and limitations of modern ZDI techniques applied to fossil fields of early-type stars. We generated synthetic spectropolarimetric data from three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of fossil magnetic fields. The resulting Stokes profiles - individual lines and least-squares deconvolved (LSD) profiles - were inverted with contemporary ZDI codes using Stokes IQUV and IV data. We compared the reconstructed maps with the input MHD surface fields and quantified deviations in field strength, vector orientation, and harmonic energy decomposition. For Stokes IQUV inversions, ZDI recovers field vector components and strength with better than 10% accuracy, while Stokes IV inversions degrade to 15-20% for the most complex geometries. The field inclination is recovered to within 10 deg, with errors increasing to 15-20 deg in the same cases. Full Stokes inversions reproduce poloidal and toroidal energies to within a few percentage points. LSD-based inversions yield accuracy comparable to, and sometimes better than, that achieved with ZDI using individual Fe II lines. Imposing a current-free poloidal constraint, which the input field satisfies, only helps where the unconstrained Stokes IV inversion performs poorly. Cross-talk between magnetic and abundance reconstructions is weak, with spurious inhomogeneities at or below 0.1 dex on average. Modern ZDI robustly reconstructs fossil magnetic fields in early-type stars, including their smaller-scale non-dipolar features, particularly when full Stokes information is available.

papers.title: Ultralight scalar field domain walls and Galileo GNSS atomic clocks
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the impact of an Earth-sized ultralight scalar field domain wall (DW) on the European Galileo Global Navigation Satellite System constellation and the feasibility of a related detection. In particular, a set of statistical procedures is developed and implemented to characterize the statistical properties of the background noise for a subnetwork of $N$ Galileo satellite clocks, including a false-alarm rate estimation and a detection efficiency analysis. These methods allow to implement a coincidence analysis and establish a preliminary statistical framework for a robust and controlled search for domain-wall crossings in clock data, and for deriving constraints on the associated fundamental particle physics parameters. The activity is addressed from the point of view of the scientific objectives of the Galileo for Science (G4S$\_2.0$) project.

papers.title: Naturalness in the Past from a Time-Dependent Supersymmetry Scale
papers.abstract: We consider the possibility that electroweak naturalness may be epoch dependent. In no-scale supergravity, a rolling quintessence modulus can control the supersymmetry-breaking scale, allowing superpartners to be much lighter in the early universe while remaining heavy today. Fifth-force and varying-constant effects can be suppressed via correlated modular weights in the visible-sector Kähler metric and modulus-dependent superpotential Yukawa couplings, while radiative stability of the quintessence potential requires additional tuning of the field-dependent vacuum energy. The resulting effective theory has distinctive implications for early-universe phase transitions, relic abundances, and gravitational waves.

papers.title: Reabsorbed Urca neutrinos suppress bulk-viscous damping of neutron star merger oscillations
papers.abstract: Reabsorption of Urca neutrinos suppresses the bulk-viscous damping predicted for neutron star merger oscillations. Below the direct-Urca threshold the capture neutrinos have mean energies of 19-46 MeV and are absorbed within metres. An energy-resolved kinetic treatment gives 2.7 s for a 1-kHz, 10-km oscillation at nuclear density and 4 MeV, against 19 ms for freely escaping neutrinos. It holds across the sampled states, three equations of state and the rate variations, with nearly frozen composition. This absorption is present in full-kinematics rates and absent from elastic opacity tables.

papers.title: Depth of Maximum of EAS and Mean Mass Composition of Primary CRs from the Spatial and Temporal Distribution of Cherenkov Light According to TAIGA-HiSCORE Data
papers.abstract: We present the dependence of the depth of maximum of extensive air showers (EAS), $X_{\max}$, on the energy of the primary particle, as determined from data recorded with the wide-angle Cherenkov array TAIGA-HiSCORE during the 2021--2025 observation seasons. The reconstruction of $X_{\max}$ from the experimental data uses relations obtained from EAS simulations: the dependence on the steepness of the Cherenkov light lateral distribution function ($P$-method) and on the full width at half maximum of the Cherenkov light pulse ($τ$-method). The reconstructed $X_{\max}$ values are converted into the mean logarithmic mass $\langle\ln A\rangle$, which characterizes the primary cosmic-ray mass composition. The results are compared with measurements from Tunka-133 (2017), the Pierre Auger Observatory (2019), LHAASO (2024), TALE (2026), and other experiments.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of the H$α$ Luminosity Functions at $z\sim 1.3$ and $z\sim 2.0$ in the CANUCS Lensing Fields with JWST NIRISS
papers.abstract: We present H$α$ luminosity function (LF) measurements at redshifts $z\sim1.3$ and $z\sim2.0$. We adopt JWST grism data in five lensing cluster fields and their parallel fields from the CANUCS program: ABELL-370, MACS-J0416, MACS-J0417, MACS-J1149, MACS-J1423. Based on emission lines spectroscopically identified in the F115W, F150W and F200W filters, our final sample consists of 762 H$α$ emitters, including 433 at $1.1<z<1.5$ and 329 at $1.8<z<2.2$. Through detailed effective volume and completeness analysis for each source, we construct the H$α$ LF in two redshift bins. Thanks to the sensitivity of NIRISS WFSS and gravitational lensing magnification, our sample reaches intrinsic H$α$ luminosities down to $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{40.6}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $L_{\rm Hα}\sim10^{41}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$ at $z\sim2.0$ with completeness larger than 80\%. The larger survey volume and coverage of multiple independent sightlines help mitigate cosmic variance. After accounting for cosmic variance, we constrain the faint-end slopes to be $α_{\mathrm{H}α}=-1.51^{+0.06}_{-0.04}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $-1.42^{+0.09}_{-0.06}$ at $z\sim2.0$, indicating a mild evolution between the two redshift bins. We find a negligible contribution from bright active galactic nuclei in our sample. We estimate integrated cosmic star formation rate densities of $0.103^{+0.008}_{-0.007}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.3$ and $0.149^{+0.016}_{-0.013}~M_{\odot}~\rm yr^{-1}~Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim2.0$. The emission-line samples presented here will enable further detailed studies of galaxy properties including metallicities. The methodology presented here can be readily applicable to other JWST slitless spectroscopic datasets and future wide-field slitless surveys, including those from Euclid, Roman, and the Chinese Space Station Telescope.

papers.title: A Self-Interacting Dark-Matter Route to Supermassive Kerr Black Holes via Super-Eddington Bondi Accretion: Mass-Spin Evolution
papers.abstract: Recent JWST observations motivate mechanisms for rapid black-hole growth in the early Universe. Extending our previous Schwarzschild study, we show that critical relativistic Bondi accretion of repulsively self-interacting dark matter remains an efficient super-Eddington channel for Kerr black holes with rotating inflow. Within a stationary equatorial quasi-spherical framework, smooth critical solutions exist over a finite range of inflow angular momentum set by the Kerr marginally bound capture values. Rotation changes the sonic structure and accretion efficiency, while the critical density cancellation and dark-sector/halo matching retain their Schwarzschild form. The resulting rapid growth persists until the finite halo supply becomes limiting. Because the inflow also carries angular momentum, stellar-mass seeds can grow and spin up simultaneously; illustrative population evolutions therefore provide a joint mass--spin route to early supermassive Kerr black holes.

papers.title: Massive cold hybrid stars in a modified Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model
papers.abstract: We propose a modified Polyakov-loop Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (mPNJL) model in which the Polyakov potential is given by an explicit dependence on the quark chemical potential, allowing it to remain finite at zero temperature and thus to describe the confinement-deconfinement transition in cold dense matter. Combining this modified quark sector with hadronic equations of state via a Maxwell construction, we find that, depending on the model parameters, the equation of state can exhibit either two phase transitions, from hadronic matter to confined quark matter and subsequently to deconfined quark matter, or a single transition directly from hadronic to deconfined quark matter or from hadronic to confined quark matter. Stable massive cold hybrid stars with only confined and/or deconfined quark phase are obtained. We systematically examine how the parameters of the modified Polyakov potential and the quark vector interactions control the location of these transitions, and find that repulsive vector interactions are essential to obtain a stable quark core. Hybrid stars with confined and/or a deconfined core can reach maximum masses above $2M_\odot$, provided a sufficiently stiff hadronic equation of state is used at low density. In the core of the maximum-mass configurations, the speed of sound shows variations at finite baryon densities, with c$_s^2(μ)$ departing from the asymptotic conformal value c$_s^2$ = 1/3 in confined core stars. These variations serve as a diagnostic of the equation-of-state stiffness while remaining fully consistent with causality and thermodynamic stability. This work establishes the qualitative role of each model parameter in shaping hybrid-star structure.

papers.title: How Neutron Star Radii Encode the Dense-Matter Equation of State and Hadron-Quark Transition
papers.abstract: We investigate how future high-precision neutron star (NS) radius measurements encode microscopic information about the dense-matter equation of state (EOS), focusing on a possible first-order hadron--quark phase transition and the resulting mass--radius topology. Within a Bayesian framework using meta-model EOSs with nine microscopic parameters, we analyze mock radius measurements $R_{1.4}=11.9\pmσ_R$ km with $σ_R=0.9$ and $0.1$ km for canonical NSs. We introduce inverse EOS--radius mappings by studying the conditional mean of each EOS parameter as a function of the model-predicted canonical radius $R_{1.4}$. Their slope measures the sensitivity of an EOS parameter to the radius, while their curvature determines the leading precision dependence of its posterior mean through the Jensen expansion. The symmetry-energy parameters $L$ (slope) and $K_{\rm sym}$ (curvature) are strongly encoded in $R_{1.4}$ and their posterior means shift appreciably with improved radius precision, whereas the higher-order hadronic parameters show stronger topology dependence. Among the transition parameters, the transition density $ρ_t$ is the most strongly encoded in $R_{1.4}$, while the energy-density jump and quark-matter sound speed are more strongly associated with the topology of the full mass--radius sequence. Since the different topologies have strongly overlapping $R_{1.4}$ distributions, even precise radius measurements cannot by themselves identify the topology or uniquely determine the high-density transition properties. These results provide a parameter-dependent hierarchy for assessing the scientific return of future high-precision radius measurements and complementary probes of high-density NS EOS.

papers.title: Gaia parallax bias via spherical harmonics: A Python tool and discussion of possible causes
papers.abstract: Parallaxes in Gaia DR3 are known to suffer from a complex set of sky-correlated and magnitude-dependent offsets or biases at the level of a few tens of $μ$as. Estimated from a sample of one million distant quasars and AGNs from the CRF catalog, the average offset is negative, but the actual distribution of this important parameter shows significant variations on the sky. We propose a practical method to evaluate the parallax correction as a function of sky position and, optionally, of $G$ magnitude using a spherical harmonic series, and supply a tested Python tool {\tt varpi3.py} available on Zenodo\footnote{ https://zenodo.org/records/21708614}. We find that only the constant $Y_{00}$ term is significantly dependent on magnitude, while the other 80 harmonic terms are either close to zero or flat with magnitude. The directions of the smallest and largest parallax offsets are $(l,b)\simeq(220\degr,+43\degr)$ and $(l,b)\simeq(45\degr,-45\degr)$, which are close to the orientation of the quasar density dipole reported in recent publications. Motivated by this curious coincidence, we review possible physical effects resulting in a negative bias of measured parallaxes, including an anisotropic universe with a positive curvature and an orbital aberration component. The proposed method of parallax correction is tested using independent asteroseismology data for four different areas on the sphere. Finally, we show that the parallax zero-point propagates into the CRF proper-motion field through the parallax--proper-motion covariance, biasing the vector spherical harmonic determination of the secular-aberration glide, and hence the Galactocentric acceleration, at the microarcsecond-per-year level.

papers.title: The Wave-Regulated Precursor of a Near-Parallel Interplanetary Shock Observed by Parker Solar Probe
papers.abstract: Diffusive shock acceleration, at shocks from coronal mass ejections to supernova-remnant blast waves, presupposes a scattering wave field that the accelerated particles themselves maintain. This self-regulation has not been resolved in situ. We report Parker Solar Probe observations of a fast (~2800 km/s), near-parallel interplanetary shock at 0.24 AU on 2023 March 13 and separate its upstream wave field into four families, a classification not made before at a fast shock near the Sun. Right-hand and left-hand circularly polarized families over a common wavenumber band, with a field-aligned linearly polarized family, are cyclotron-resonant with the suprathermal-to-MeV protons streaming from the shock: the beam drives the field that scatters it, and the measured mean free path, half the precursor scale, leaves the beam anisotropic enough to sustain the drive. Outside this loop lies a weak, oblique, linearly polarized component, a few per cent of the wave power, resolved here for the first time at an in situ foreshock. Its in-phase density and field-magnitude fluctuations identify the compressive part as fast magnetosonic and shift the cyclotron-resonance energies of the resonant families by up to 13 % along the precursor. Acceleration at shocks inside 0.3 AU is governed upstream, in a foreshock the shock builds for itself.

papers.title: Observing Co-Located Neutral and Ionized Gas-Phase Iron Depletion in the Magellanic Clouds
papers.abstract: Depletion is the observed phenomenon where gas-phase elemental abundances are reduced through accretion onto dust grains. We measure neutral gas-phase elemental abundances (S, Fe) in the Magellanic Clouds along 33 sightlines using high-resolution UV spectroscopy (HST/COS and HST/STIS), and compare them to ionized gas-phase abundances (S, Fe) adopted from the literature for six co-located H\,\textsc{ii} regions (with the furthest separation of $\lesssim3'$, 50 pc). Comparing S abundances show that S is minimally depleted in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions and surrounding diffuse ISM. However, we find that the gas-phase Fe abundances in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be lower than those of the neighboring neutral ISM by 0.3 to 2 dex. This difference is likely an offset in the amount of Fe depleted into dust grains. As accretion of gas-phase Fe is likely not effective at the temperatures of the H\,\textsc{ii} regions, Fe depletion into solid form would have occurred in the dense atomic or molecular clouds prior to star formation. Stronger depletion in the H\,\textsc{ii} regions shows that Fe-bearing grains survive destruction in the first few million years following ionization. Our observations highlight that Fe depletion in H\,\textsc{ii} regions can be a useful tracer of Fe depletion in dense molecular clouds, which are challenging to observe directly via UV absorption.

papers.title: Large-Scale Dynamos Driven by Shear-Flow-Induced Jets
papers.abstract: At every scale they occupy, magnetic fields affect various phenomena, including star formation, cosmic ray transport, charged particle acceleration, space weather, transport in planetary atmospheres, and laboratory plasmas. These fields are often generated and sustained by turbulent flows in a process called the dynamo. In 1955, E. N. Parker parameterized the effects of small-scale turbulence to propose a mean-field dynamo theory. The widely used theory reproduces observed large-scale fields but suffers from difficulty in tuning parameters as they are not justified from first principles: Studies of turbulent flows show tangled magnetic fields, which are folded and fragmented into small-scale structures due to shear-flow straining. Here, considering a shear flow that is unstable and driven, we develop analytic theory and perform three-dimensional (3D), advanced computer simulations of turbulence with up to 4096 x 4096 x 8192 grid points, showing ab initio generation of quasi-periodic, large-scale magnetic fields. The generation occurs via the mean-vorticity effect---an additional mean-field dynamo process postulated in 1990. Crucial to this dynamo is the prior generation of large-scale 3D jets, robustly produced as topologically protected and exact nonlinear solutions of the magnetohydrodynamic equations. The jet-driven dynamo applies to shear-driven laboratory and astrophysical systems. These include binary neutron star mergers, where the reported dynamo likely operates on microsecond timescales to produce in milliseconds some of the strongest magnetic fields in the Universe, providing signals for multimessenger astronomy.

papers.title: 3D Radiative Transfer of Lyman-series Lines with SKIRT
papers.abstract: Context. High-resolution X-ray spectroscopy and polarimetry provided by XRISM and IXPE offer new diagnostics of the geometry and kinematics of photo-ionised plasmas around compact objects. Interpreting reprocessed X-ray emission in such systems requires full three-dimensional radiative transfer (3D RT) including photon-ion interactions. Aims. We extend the Monte Carlo (MC) RT code SKIRT by implementing the Lyman-series lines of H-like ions, enabling self-consistent modelling of resonance scattering, radiative recombination, and polarisation of these lines in X-ray photo-ionised plasmas. Methods. We implemented Lyman-series transitions (up to $n=10$) for ions with $Z=$1--30, including fine-structure splitting and linear polarisation in resonance scattering. Two channels for the production of the Lyman-series lines (resonance scattering and radiative recombination) are considered. Results. The implementation reproduces analytical expectations and shows good agreement with Cloudy. The SKIRT simulations naturally capture RT effects such as P Cygni profiles and line-profile distortion in optically thick media, which are inaccessible to the conventional 1D RT codes commonly used in X-rays. In 3D geometries, we find that anisotropic illumination and velocity fields significantly modify the Lyman series line ratios and profiles, all of which are observable with XRISM. Conclusions. The extended version of SKIRT provides a powerful framework for interpreting X-ray line spectra and polarisation from photo-ionised plasmas. It is particularly suited for constraining the geometry and velocity structure in the vicinity of compact objects in the XRISM and IXPE era.

papers.title: CosmoFit: A Graphical User Interface for Bayesian Cosmological Parameter Estimation with User-Defined H(z) Models
papers.abstract: We present CosmoFit, a desktop graphical interface for Bayesian parameter inference in background cosmology. The application is designed to simplify cosmological analyses by reducing the need to manually program each step, while maintaining the transparency and reproducibility of the results. Users can define an expansion history H(z), specify fixed and sampled parameters, assign prior ranges and proposal scales, select the available observational likelihoods, and run Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses from a unified graphical interface. CosmoFit uses Cobaya for Bayesian sampling and GetDist for posterior analysis and visualization. The current version supports cosmic-chronometer data and the official Pantheon+, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union3 supernova likelihoods available through Cobaya. For each run, the application stores the configuration files, metadata, execution logs, chains, and numerical summaries required to inspect and reproduce the analysis. The performance of CosmoFit was evaluated through unit tests, a parameter-recovery test using synthetic data, and an independent comparison with an analysis performed directly in Cobaya. The posterior mean values obtained with both procedures agree to within less than one percent. In addition, the synthetic-data test recovers the fiducial parameters within the expected credible regions. As an illustrative example, we perform a spatially flat wCDM analysis using Pantheon+SH0ES and obtain marginalized constraints and triangle plots directly from the interface. Within its current scope, CosmoFit provides an accessible, transparent, and reproducible tool for research and academic applications involving explicit models of the background cosmological expansion.

papers.title: Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis
papers.abstract: We propose a low-scale spontaneous leptogenesis scenario within the dynamical minimal scotogenic model for accommodating neutrino masses and inert scalar dark matter simultaneously. Thus, we dub the mechanism Spontaneous Scoto-leptogenesis. In this setup, a rolling Majoron arising from the global $U(1)_{B-L}$ symmetry breaking induces an effective chemical potential for the $B-L$ charge in the presence of $B-L$ violating interactions that allow for the efficient decays and inverse decays of right handed neutrinos (RHN) and RHN mediated scattering, so it gives rise to the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe through the electroweak sphaleron conversion. The mechanism becomes effective in the strong washout regime and successfully lowers the viable mass scale of the lightest RHN to the range of TeV scales, thereby making the thermal scotogenic leptogenesis with two hierarchical RHNs accessible to direct tests. We identify the roles of the $λ_5$ coupling for spontaneous leptogenesis and inert scalar dark matter through the efficient erasure of the inert scalar asymmetry. We also explore the regime for Majoron dark matter from the kinetic misalignment, showing that a multicomponent dark sector comprising the inert scalar and the Majoron can be realized in the model. The resulting framework provides a unified origin for low-scale baryogenesis, neutrino masses, and multicomponent dark sector, so it can be tested by complementary experimental probes through direct detection experiments, collider searches for inert scalars, and future detection of Majoron dark matter or dark radiation.

papers.title: Ripples in the OCEANS: Broad Line Variability of Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are a unique class of compact, red sources discovered in the JWST extragalactic deep fields. Determining if they are indeed powered by accreting supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is one of the main drivers of the intense study of these objects. Evidence for variability in these objects provides a direct test for the active galactic nucleus (AGN) nature of their central engine. In this study, we present a variability analysis of 6 LRDs observed by the $R \sim 2700$ OCEANS survey and leverage archival $R \sim 1000$ spectroscopic data from the CEERS and RUBIES surveys. We report marginal detections of $\rm Hα$ broad-line (BL) variability in the LRDs OCEANS-100424/RUBIES-42232 (27\% variability at 2.1$σ$ significance) and OCEANS-35829/RUBIES-49140 (GlimmIr/Irony; 50\% variability at 1.5$σ$ significance). The other 4 LRDs in our sample do not show evidence for BL variability, with a 1$σ$ upper limit of $4.8 \% - 30\%$ variability between their epochs of observations. We also find no evidence ($<1σ$) for continuum variability in our LRD sample. We compare our results to a sample of SDSS-RM quasars to determine the probability of our broad $\rm Hα$ variability detections. We find that the probability of reproducing 2 variable and 4 nonvariable quasars is $4.71\%$, corresponding to $\sim 2 σ$ departure from typical quasar variability. The detection of BL $\rm Hα$ variability in 2 LRDs provides some evidence for the AGN nature of these objects as opposed to pure scattering models.

papers.title: Singlet-Doublet fermion origin of dark matter, neutrino mass and inverse first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: We study the possibility of an inverse first-order electroweak phase transition (IFOEWPT) and observable gravitational waves (GW) in a radiative neutrino mass model of scotogenic type where singlet-doublet (SD) fermions, the lightest of whom is the dark matter (DM) candidate, generate the necessary seesaw at one-loop level. Considering the possibility of light neutrinos being Dirac for simplicity and additional detection prospects, we extend the standard model (SM) with two generations of $SU(2)_L$ singlet and doublet fermions, one singlet scalar, and three right-handed neutrinos (RHNs). While RHNs provide the right chiral parts of light Dirac neutrinos, the SD fermions and the scalar singlet facilitate the one-loop neutrino mass diagram. The neutral component of the lighter SD fermion, stabilized under a residual $Z_2$ symmetry plays the role of DM while the heavier SD fermions strongly couple to the Higgs leading to an IFOEWPT where the Universe undergoes two different first-order phase transition as it goes from the symmetric to the final broken Higgs phase. We constrain the parameter space from the requirements of generating the correct neutrino mass, DM relic as well as IFOEWPT while incorporating the existing constraints from different experiments. The final allowed parameter space of the model can be probed at collider, direct-detection, GW and cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments in near future.

papers.title: CLASSY. XV. Kinematics and Spatial Distributions of Outflows in Local Highly Star-Forming Galaxies
papers.abstract: Star-forming galaxies drive massive outflows that play an important role in galaxy evolution by regulating feedback and influencing the dynamics of surrounding media. Measuring galactic outflow rates is essential for quantifying feedback efficiency and the amount of mass, momentum, and energy deposited into the circumgalactic medium. In this paper, we examine 17 galactic outflows from the CLASSY survey with radiative transfer modeling of UV absorption lines presented in M. Huberty et al. (2024), to study their spatial distributions and kinematic properties. We study the SiII, SiIII, and SiIV ionization states that trace the cool and warm phases of the outflows and find that SiII traced winds generally behave differently than the warmer SiIII and SiIV traced winds. We derive the mass, momentum, and energy loading factors, which we find scale inversely proportional to stellar mass. We find that our measurements of the mass and momentum loading factors are in agreement with the hydrodynamic FIRE-2 simulations. We model the velocity profiles of the winds, with profiles reaching a maximum velocity of 620 km/s on average, in agreement with hydrodynamic simulations from CGOLS. We also investigate the relationship between outflow properties and the age of the stellar population from SED fitting. We find that outflows associated with young star forming regions are more likely to have a column density dominated by cooler gas and have mass outflow rates which decrease with radius.

papers.title: Astronomical Cardiology II: A Search For Heartbeat Stars Using APOGEE and TESS
papers.abstract: Stellar binaries in short-period, highly eccentric systems with significant tidal deformations near pericenter, also known as heartbeat stars, are a laboratory for studying dynamical tides and oscillations in stars. We identify 50 heartbeat stars using TESS light curves of stars identified as binaries using SDSS APOGEE. We fit their phase-folded TESS light curves with an analytic model to measure their orbital periods, eccentricities, inclinations, and arguments of periastron. We measure the mass function of targets with enough APOGEE radial velocity observations to obtain a constraint on the secondary mass. We confirm our previous results that the non-giant heartbeat stars have started to evolve off the main sequence and that the fraction of (near) main sequence binaries that are heartbeat stars rises rapidly with effective temperature.

papers.title: Trace the Self-Gravitating Gas Using CO Isotopologues
papers.abstract: Recent studies have shown that the star formation rate (SFR) correlates tightly and linearly with the mass of gravitationally bound gas, which can be delineated from the power-law tail of the column-density probability distribution function ($N$-PDF) derived from dust emission observations. This relationship holds across four orders of magnitude within the Milky Way--spanning low-mass to high-mass star-forming regions and encompassing the extreme environment of the Central Molecular Zone. Building on this framework, we present a new approach for estimating the mass of gravitationally bound gas in molecular clouds using multi-line CO isotopologue observations. Our sample includes 16 molecular clouds with robust detections in $^{12}$CO, $^{13}$CO, and C$^{18}$O $J$ = 1-0, spanning both massive inner Galaxy clouds and nearby star-forming regions. We find that the $N$-PDFs derived from combined CO isotopologue data recover the characteristic log-normal plus power-law profiles seen in dust-based studies. The mass and spatial distribution of the self-gravitating structures estimated from both dust-based and CO-based methods agree well throughout the sample. This indicates that the CO isotopologue combination can robustly trace the self-gravitating component via the $N$-PDF method and provides a reliable, scalable, and velocity-resolved alternative to dust emission for identifying the star-forming gas in molecular clouds.

papers.title: FLAGS II: Constraining Galaxy Formation Models with Dimensionality Reduction of Direct Observables
papers.abstract: Comparisons between observations of galaxies and theoretical predictions are regularly performed using physical properties, which are inferred by the often slow and biased process of SED fitting. Forward modelling facilitates a reliable alternative, whereby models are evaluated using direct observables alone. However, these datasets become high-dimensional when collating observations from multiple telescopes, leading to sparse sampling, memory intensity and visualisation difficulties. We show that 2D embeddings of JWST and HST photometric fluxes, constructed using the non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm UMAP, preserve sufficient information to differentiate between five models. Using a simple $χ^{2}$-like metric, we show that JAGUAR reproduces the population of bright galaxies $(m_{\mathrm{AB}}<26)$ in GOODS-S six times as well as SC-SAM and twelve times as well as SAGE. By adjusting the hyperparameters, we quantify how well each model replicates the distribution of SED shapes. The template SED approach of SPRITZ and the lack of photoionisation in SAGE cause significant discrepancies, highlighting the importance of comprehensive forward modelling. The embedded position of each galaxy can be identified $>100$ times faster than inferring its properties with Bayesian SED fitting, making this approach an ideal alternative for deriving statistical model constraints from large surveys such as LSST and Euclid, and performing simulation-based inference with CAMELS.

papers.title: Thermal false vacuum decay near black holes is aspherical
papers.abstract: We study decay of a scalar field false vacuum near a (3+1)-dimensional Schwarzschild black hole equilibrated at Hawking temperature with the environment. Our scalar field model has negative quartic self-coupling and thereby resembles Higgs sector of the Standard Model in the large-field limit. We demonstrate that if the black hole is not too small, the false vacuum in this model decays aspherically with regard to the black hole center: via formation of expanding true vacuum bubbles emerging on the outer side of the event horizon. More specifically, we identify three regimes of the decay. For the largest and coldest black holes, the main mechanism is quantum tunneling described by an infinitesimally thin bounce sitting at some point of the horizon. In the intermediate-mass regime, the vacuum is destroyed by thermal fluctuations creating aspherical critical bubbles in the horizon vicinity. Finally, near the smallest black holes thermal fluctuations still guide the decay but the dominant critical bubble is spherically symmetric and covers the entire horizon.

papers.title: Why is GN-z11 Bright, Compact, and Nitrogen Enhanced? Insights from UV Absorption and Emission Diagnostics
papers.abstract: We investigate the UV spectrum of GN-z11, a luminous, compact galaxy with strong nitrogen lines, at $z=10.60$, using deep JWST/NIRSpec high-resolution IFU and medium-resolution MSA spectra assembled from the JADES, SPURS, and GO programs. After optimized reduction and extraction of the IFU data including an evaluation of statistical and systematic uncertainties, we obtain mutually consistent spectra from the high- and medium-resolution observations. After carefully accounting for the data quality limitations, we identify prominent P-Cygni profiles in NV$λ\lambda1238,1243$, SiIV$λ\lambda1394,1403$, and CIV$λ\lambda1548,1550$, together with broad NIV]$λ\lambda1483,1486$ emission (FWHM $\sim1600$ km s$^{-1}$). The P-Cygni profiles resemble those of massive stars such as O-type stars and luminous blue variables (LBVs), while the broad NIV] emission resembles that of nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) stars. We fit stellar and active galactic nuclei (AGN) UV spectral models and find that the stellar models are strongly preferred over the AGN models ($Δ$WAIC $=-20$), with the preference driven primarily by the NV P-Cygni profile. These results indicate that the luminous, compact UV continuum of GN-z11 is dominated by massive stars. We derive electron densities from CIII]$λ\lambda1907,1909$, NIII]$λ\lambda1747-1754$, and NIV], with the nitrogen diagnostics extending well beyond the CIII]-based limit and reaching densities of $\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ for NIV], indicating physically distinct carbon- and nitrogen-emitting nebular components. These findings suggest that the apparent nitrogen enhancement inferred for GN-z11 as a whole may arise when strong narrow nitrogen emission originates from dense gas locally enriched in nitrogen by WN stellar winds and photoionized by nearby massive stars within the same star-forming region.

papers.title: Interacting Supernovae: a Radio and X-ray Strategy to Constrain the Structure of the Circumstellar Medium
papers.abstract: The interaction of supernova (SN) ejecta with the dense circumstellar medium (CSM) converts shock kinetic energy into radiation across multiple wavebands. We investigate the dependence of the X-ray and radio emission on the CSM geometry, considering spherical, hourglass, and disk shapes for the CSM. We find that the spectral and light-curve properties, both in X-ray and radio, significantly differ for spherical and non-spherical CSM structures. For a non-spherical CSM, the radio light curve flattens out near the peak frequency, due to efficient free-free absorption by the unshocked CSM. Moreover, the early rise of the radio light curve is shallower when the CSM density along the observer line of sight is larger than that in other directions. If the CSM density is lower along the observer line of sight, the radio light curve flattens near its peak, and the reverse-shock component is negligible in X-rays. Building on these features, we provide a method to constrain the CSM structure based on the rising part the radio light curve in the proximity of its peak; we show that the decay part of the radio light curve, after its peak, carries insight on whether the CSM density profile is wind-like or not. We further adopt the X-ray signal to corroborate the information extracted from radio. We test our strategy on SN 1993j and SN 2023ixf. For both SNe, we find that an asymmetric CSM is in excellent agreement with radio and X-ray observations and provides a viable alternative to non-wind scenarios suggested in the literature. Our findings highlight the crucial insight provided by radio and X-ray signals into the mass-loss history of the SN progenitor.

papers.title: Recycled Gas Dominates the Metal-rich Fuel of Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Understanding the origin and chemical properties of gas accreted by supermassive black holes (SMBHs) is essential for linking black hole growth to galaxy evolution. Using a suite of 30 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations, we investigate the chemical properties of gas accreted onto SMBHs in massive galaxies with stellar masses of $10^{10.9-11.9}\,\rm M_\odot$ and black hole masses of $10^{8.5-9.7}\,\rm M_\odot$ at $z=0$. By tracing the full cosmological histories of individual gas particles, we identify their origins and enrichment pathways. The accreted gas is classified into four categories: ``early'' gas accreted during the early assembly phase of the main halo, ``external'' gas originating from other galaxies or subhalos, ``recycled'' gas enriched through stellar evolution processes within the primary galaxy, including asymptotic giant branch (AGB) winds and supernova ejecta, and ``smooth'' gas accreted from the intergalactic medium. We find that recycled gas dominates the accretion budget and is already metal rich at early epochs. Gas from other origins typically undergoes gradual chemical enrichment within the galactic environment prior to black hole accretion. The mean abundance ratios show only weak redshift evolution and are broadly compatible with the high metallicities inferred for quasar broad-line regions. Our results suggest that metal-rich gas supply to SMBHs arises naturally from cosmological galaxy evolution and stellar recycling.

papers.title: The Ĝ Infrared Search for Extraterrestrial Civilizations with Large Energy Supplies. V. When Galaxies Glow with Industry
papers.abstract: We present the most robust stellar population synthesis (SPS)-based search for galaxy-spanning technological waste heat to date, applied to 129 nearby galaxies spanning a wide range of spectral energy distribution (SED) types, including ultraluminous IR galaxies and MIR-luminous active galactic nuclei (AGN). We incorporate the AGENT Dyson sphere formalism into the Flexible Stellar Population Synthesis code at the stellar population level, so nebular and dust emission respond self-consistently to Dyson sphere reprocessing.
